name: North Dakota

agency.name: North Dakota Department of Environmental Quality (NDDEQ)

overview: North Dakota uses a two-step system: a Permit to Construct (PTC) before building or modifying a source in a designated category (NDAC 33.1-15-14), then a Permit to Operate (PTO) issued after DEQ inspects the facility. Sources are classed as true minor, synthetic minor (federally enforceable limits), Title V major, and PSD major. North Dakota is in attainment for all criteria pollutants, so major preconstruction review is PSD. Oil and gas production facilities use a General Permit (GP-OG) filed through CERIS-ND. Applications and reports are filed electronically through CERIS-ND. Indian country is outside the GP-OG and NDDEQ's jurisdiction.

permitTypes.name: Exempt sources
permitTypes.description: Sources exempt from a PTC are listed in NDAC 33.1-15-14-02.13. For some minor-impact sources, an applicant may file and DEQ will decide in writing whether a permit is needed.

permitTypes.name: Minor Source Permit to Construct and Permit to Operate
permitTypes.description: PTC required before construction or modification; PTO issued after inspection confirms the facility was built per the PTC. Notify DEQ within 30 days of initial operation. A PTC lapses if construction does not start within 18 months unless extended. True minors generally do not need public comment.
permitTypes.quote: A true minor source Construction Permit is issued to facilities that have the potential to emit less than 100 ton/yr of a criteria pollutant, less than 10 ton/yr of any single hazardous air pollutant and less than 25 ton/yr of any combination of hazardous air pollutants.

permitTypes.name: Synthetic Minor PTC and PTO
permitTypes.description: For sources whose potential emissions are at or above major levels that accept federally enforceable limits to stay below them. Initial synthetic minor PTCs require a 30-day public comment period.

permitTypes.name: Oil and Gas General Permit (GP-OG)
permitTypes.description: General permit for oil and gas production facilities outside Indian country, filed through CERIS-ND. See the Oil and Gas section.
permitTypes.thresholds: Facility-wide criteria pollutant PTE below 250 tpy, excluding fugitives (restated from DEQ).

permitTypes.name: Prevention of Significant Deterioration (PSD) Permit to Construct
permitTypes.description: For new major sources and major modifications (all of ND is attainment/unclassifiable). Requires BACT, air quality analysis, additional impacts analysis, and a 30-day public comment period.
permitTypes.thresholds: 100 tons/yr for the listed source categories and 250 tons/yr for other sources, criteria pollutants only (restated from the DEQ permitting page).

permitTypes.name: Title V Permit to Operate
permitTypes.description: Major source operating permit, also required for some sources due to PSD applicability or Title IV Acid Rain. Initial issuance, renewals, and significant modifications need 30-day public comment, 45-day EPA review, and affected state review where applicable.
permitTypes.thresholds: At or above 100 tons/yr of a criteria pollutant, 25 tons/yr combined HAP, or 10 tons/yr of a single HAP (restated from the DEQ permitting page table).

oilAndGas.summary: North Dakota (Bakken) has a dedicated oil and gas air program. Upstream operators submit the GP-OG Application / Well Registration through CERIS-ND before well completion, then a startup notification and a Potential to Emit (PTE) report. The GP-OG is a synthetic minor permit that keeps facilities below PSD. Storage tank control is under NDAC 33.1-15-07-02.1; flares must meet NDAC 33.1-15-07-02, 33.1-15-03-03.1, 33.1-15-20, and 40 CFR 60.18. DEQ implements NSPS OOOO/OOOOa reporting. Flared gas volumes are regulated separately by the ND Industrial Commission.

programs.name: Air Oil & Gas General Permit Application / Well Registration (GP-OG)
programs.description: Required for new and modified production facilities and new or recompleted wells. Startup of production notification is due within 30 days (measured from the final well), and the facility PTE Report within 90 days of startup. Sweetening units need site-specific permits.
programs.quote: No later than two days prior to any planned well completion activities.
programs.thresholds: Facility-wide criteria pollutant PTE below 250 tpy, excluding fugitives (restated from DEQ).

programs.name: Well site and tank controls
programs.description: DEQ's Oil & Gas pages require new wells to have at least a pit flare on first production, and higher-emitting tanks need more efficient controls operating within 60 days of first production. Flares need an automatic igniter or continuous pilot.
programs.thresholds: Pit flare with 90% destruction and removal efficiency; tanks emitting more than 20 tpy VOC need more efficient controls (restated from DEQ).

programs.name: Title V and PSD triggers for production facilities
programs.description: Facilities must notify DEQ within 60 days of exceeding Title V thresholds and apply within 12 months; PSD exceedance notification is due the first business day after the exceedance is determined.
